variables-easy.title: Add a bonus
variables-easy.prompt: Write add_bonus(score) so it returns the starting score plus 10.
variables-easy.hint: Keep the input score and add exactly 10.

variables-medium.title: Convert stored text
variables-medium.prompt: Write add_five(raw) so raw is converted from text to a number, then increased by 5.
variables-medium.hint: Convert raw with int before doing arithmetic.

variables-hard.title: Copy before changing
variables-hard.prompt: Write copy_and_add(values) so it returns a new list with 99 appended, without changing values.
variables-hard.hint: Use values.copy(), append to the copy, and return the copy.

conditions-easy.title: Choose an age label
conditions-easy.prompt: Write age_label(age) so it returns 'adult' for ages 18 and over, otherwise 'minor'.
conditions-easy.hint: The boundary age 18 belongs in the adult branch.

conditions-medium.title: Choose free shipping
conditions-medium.prompt: Write shipping_cost(total, member). Return 0 when total is at least 50 or member is True; otherwise return 5.
conditions-medium.hint: Combine the two requirements with or.

conditions-hard.title: Guard a division
conditions-hard.prompt: Write safe_ratio(total, count). Return None when count is 0; otherwise return total / count.
conditions-hard.hint: Check count before division so the zero case never divides.

loops-easy.title: Add through the endpoint
loops-easy.prompt: Write inclusive_sum(n) so it returns the sum of every whole number from 1 through n.
loops-easy.starterCode:
def inclusive_sum(n):
    total = 0
    # Add every number through n
    return total
loops-easy.hint: range stops before its second argument.

loops-medium.title: Move a while loop
loops-medium.prompt: Write countdown_total(start) so it sums start down through 1 and terminates.
loops-medium.starterCode:
def countdown_total(start):
    current = start
    total = 0
    while current > 0:
        # Add current and move toward zero
        pass
    return total
loops-medium.hint: Update both the total and the loop-control variable.

loops-hard.title: Count a nested grid
loops-hard.prompt: Write grid_visits(rows, columns) using nested loops to return how many cells are visited.
loops-hard.starterCode:
def grid_visits(rows, columns):
    count = 0
    # Visit each column in each row
    return count
loops-hard.hint: The inner loop runs once for every outer-loop iteration.

lists-easy.title: Add every item
lists-easy.prompt: Write add_items(values) so it returns the sum of every value in the list.
lists-easy.starterCode:
def add_items(values):
    total = 0
    # Visit every item
    return total
lists-easy.hint: A for item in values loop visits the values directly.

lists-medium.title: Slice out the middle
lists-medium.prompt: Write middle_items(values) so it returns a list without the first and last items.
lists-medium.hint: A slice can omit the first item and exclude the last boundary.

lists-hard.title: Copy before appending
lists-hard.prompt: Write lengths_after_copy(values). Copy the list, append 0 to the copy, and return [len(values), len(copy)].
lists-hard.hint: Assignment aliases a list; .copy() creates a separate outer list.

functions-easy.title: Return a doubled value
functions-easy.prompt: Write double(number) so it returns number multiplied by 2.
functions-easy.hint: Return the expression; printing it does not send it to the caller.

functions-medium.title: Use a default argument
functions-medium.prompt: Write final_price(price, discount=0) so it returns price minus discount.
functions-medium.hint: Use both parameters in the returned expression.

functions-hard.title: Avoid a shared default list
functions-hard.prompt: Write collect(item, bag=None). Create a new list when bag is None, append item, and return the list.
functions-hard.hint: Use None as the default, then create the list inside the function.
